source.publisher: Northern Whig (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: names, divisions and party labels read on the page image of the Northern Whig nominations report of 3 May 1930 and checked against the Mid-Ulster Mail

note: Nomination-day report for the twenty-six divisions of Magherafelt rural district, one member each. No division was contested: twenty-four candidates were returned unopposed and the retiring members for Bancran and Tullykeeran were returned without nomination. Party labels are those printed in the Northern Whig report. The round is filed on the rural districts' polling day in early June 1930 (queue nominal 29 May). Sole nomination; returned unopposed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Brackaslievegallion' to Brackagh Slieve Gallion (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Magherafelt Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Brackagh Slieve Gallion; the rounds were filed as Brackaghslievegallion (1927, 1936, 1946, 1949, 1952, 1955, 1961, 1964, 1967); Brackaslievegallion (1930, 1933, 1939); Brackaghslievegallon (1958). This round was filed as 'Brackaslievegallion', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (brackaslievegallion) answers with a redirect to this one.
